(01:12:02): For those who really... And there are people who really get hung up on the .com, they tend to older by, the way. And have, in their mind, sort of the hotness of the internet and having a .com, which did make a difference 25 years ago. But it's 25 years now or 30, right? The good news is because they're less valuable, you can typically buy a URL if you negotiate the right way and have time for 15, 20, 25, $30,000. And we say, "Hey, if you can do that, have fun. I'd put the $30,000 into market."
turns.zh: 太高兴你问这个了，因为到今天，它根本不重要。.com 或 URL 地址已经变成了"区号"。你在 415 还是 615，人们根本不在乎。而现在有了 AI，SEO 也会越来越不重要。所以我只认一个原则：你得先把对的名字拿到手。然后如果你能拿到 .com，当然去拿。但如果拿不到，有绕过去的办法——你可以在前面加个前缀、前面或后面加个小词，或者去用 .ai 之类的。但核心原则是：先把对的名字拿到手。（01:12:02）那些真的……确实有人特别纠结 .com，顺便说，他们往往年纪偏大。他们脑子里还留着互联网最火那会儿、有个 .com 很重要的印象，而那在 25 年前确实重要。但那都是 25 年、30 年前的事了，对吧？好消息是，正因为它们没那么值钱了，你通常能买到一个 URL——只要你会谈、有耐心——花个 1.5 万、2 万、2.5 万、3 万美元。我们会说："嘿，你要能搞定，玩去吧。但我宁可把那 3 万美元投到市场上。"

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. That's reassuring. I imagine many founders are just like, "God dammit, there's no names available anymore." Let me zoom out and just ask you this question as a, maybe, a closing thought to our conversation. (01:12:56): Say you were just in an elevator ride with someone, and I'm sure this happens to you of just like, "Hey, David, I got to come up with that name. What's your biggest tip for coming up with a great name?" What would your answer be?
turns.zh: 太棒了。这让人安心。我猜很多创始人就是"该死，现在根本没名字可用了"。让我把镜头拉远，问你一个——也许作为我们对话的收尾。（01:12:56）假设你正和某人在电梯里，我肯定这种事常发生在你身上："嘿 David，我得想出那个名字。你取个好名字最大的建议是什么？"你会怎么回答？

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: I'd go back to forget about the word, think about behavior and experience. And then the second thing from just a creative help, I'm a big believer in synchronicity. And we try to force synchronicity here, and I'll give you a couple examples of that. But this idea of connecting dots, two unrelated ideas together. And so I'll say, "Look, if someone says we make sailboats and I'm trying to..." I'm here in Sausalito. I guess, that's why I thought about that. And I am trying to create a new name for my company that builds sailboats. (01:13:49): I would say forget about sailboats. I would go and pick out some magazines about hunting or flying magazines. And I would just look through those, get a notepad out, and put out words that you like. Things, expressions that you like. And then that synchronicity, I said, "I would bet you $5 that out of those two magazines, you will get a word that you never would've thought of, but somehow it would relate to sailing."
turns.zh: 我会回到那句话：忘掉那个"词"，去想行为和体验。然后第二点，从创意帮助的角度，我非常相信"共时性"（synchronicity）。我们在这里会刻意制造共时性，我给你举几个例子。就是那种把两个不相干的点连起来的想法。所以我会说："看，如果有人说我们造帆船，而我正试着……"我在 Sausalito，我想就是因为这才想到这个。我正试着为我这家造帆船的公司想个新名字。（01:13:49）我会说：忘掉帆船。去挑几本关于狩猎、或者飞行的杂志。翻一翻，拿个本子，把你看中的词、喜欢的表达记下来。然后那种共时性——我会说："我跟你赌 5 美元，从那两本杂志里，你会蹦出一个你绝不会想到的词，但它 somehow 会和航海扯上关系。"

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That connects very much to your story of how you have these different teams, and the teams that end up coming up with a winning name are the ones thinking about a very different version of that product.
turns.zh: 这和你的故事特别呼应——你们那些不同的团队，最后想出获胜名字的，恰恰是那些在想这个产品一个非常不同版本的团队。

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So interesting. Okay. David, this was everything I was hoping it'd be. I feel like we're going to help so many people. Is there anything that we haven't covered or that you want to leave listeners with as a final nugget or piece of advice or story before we get to our very exciting lightning round?
turns.zh: 太有意思了。好。David，这期完全就是我期待的样子。我觉得我们能帮到太多人了。在我们进入超精彩的快问快答之前，还有什么没聊到的，或者你想留给听众的最后一点建议、故事？

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: I'm going to emphasize one point, I think, which is that I really would like the listeners to really begin to think about how valuable a brand name can be. That you're not just looking for a word, you're looking for this experience. And if you get it right, not just a good name but the right name, the value is almost unlimited. And so give yourself some time, give yourself a budget, give yourself the right resources to do that. Second thing is we try to really be helpful here, and so I am always happy to talk to people about where they are in a process and if we can help, or just give them a little bit of advice. And we schedule, we call them office hours here. We're judicious about it, but we are open to that. It's just playing a long-term game, so I'd like to leave that with the viewers also.
turns.zh: 我想强调一点：我真心希望听众开始意识到，一个品牌名能有多值钱。你找的不只是一个词，你找的是一种体验。如果你做对了——不只是一个好名字，而是对的名字——那价值几乎是无尽的。所以，给自己一点时间，给自己一笔预算，给自己对的资源去做这件事。第二点是，我们真的很想帮忙，所以我永远乐意和人聊他们流程走到哪了、我们能不能帮上忙，或者就给他们一点建议。我们会安排，我们叫它"答疑时间"（office hours）。我们对此很慎重，但确实是开放的。这只是一场长期游戏，所以我也想把这点留给观众。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: We're about to book out your office hours. I love that offer. I think a lot of people are going to take advantage of that. That is super cool. (01:15:58): David, with that, we've reached our very exciting lightning round. I've got five questions for you. Are you ready?
turns.zh: 我们马上要把你的答疑时间约满了。我太喜欢这个提议了。我觉得很多人会去用。这太酷了。（01:15:58）David，说到这儿，我们进入了超精彩的快问快答环节。我有五个问题给你。准备好了吗？

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: Yes, I'm ready.
turns.zh: 准备好了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There we go. What are 2 or 3 books that you find yourself recommending most to other people?
turns.zh: 来了。你最常推荐给别人的两三本书是什么？

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: There's a book called Resilience, which was written by a former Navy SEAL that... And it's not about combat, it's just a tiny bit about being a SEAL. But it is about overcoming things and it's about tenacity. And I think everybody in the world, we all have challenges and things. And I do recommend that to people. (01:16:31): Second book is Andrew Roberts latest book on Winston Churchill. Winston Churchill is, really, one of my heroes. He was one of the most unusual, provocative statesmen/politicians of the 20th century. And here's another person that talked about tenacity, and ups and downs, and stick with it. And so, I do like to recommend that. Some people just tipped their head and said, "Ah, I don't know." It seems like maybe a boring book, but those are two books that I [inaudible 01:17:02].
turns.zh: 有一本书叫《Resilience》（韧性），是一个前海豹突击队队员写的……它不聊战斗，只略微提到当 SEAL 的经历。但它讲的是克服困难，讲的是韧劲。我觉得这世上每个人都有挑战和难事，所以我确实会推荐这本书。（01:16:31）第二本是 Andrew Roberts 写丘吉尔的最新那本。丘吉尔真的是我的英雄之一。他是 20 世纪最不寻常、最有挑衅意味的政治家之一。又是一个大谈韧劲、起起落落、坚持到底的人。所以我也很喜欢推荐这本。有些人只是歪着头说"啊，我不知道"，好像觉得这可能是本无聊的书，但这两本就是我会〔听不清 01:17:02〕的书。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Who would ever say that Churchill's story is boring? That's absurd.
turns.zh: 谁会说丘吉尔的故事无聊？那也太离谱了。

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: I think so. I agree. I agree It's absurd, yes.
turns.zh: 我也这么想。我同意。确实离谱，没错。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: He's so fascinating. There's a recent documentary, I think, that really showed me the character. Incredible. (01:17:18): Okay. What's a recent movie or TV show you've really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 他太有魅力了。最近有部纪录片，我觉得真的把他的性格展现出来了。了不起。（01:17:18）好。最近有哪部电影或剧集你特别喜欢？

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: For me, it's the Yellowstone series. We're very fortunate as a family, we have some property in Montana. And-
turns.zh: 对我来说，是《黄石》（Yellowstone）系列。我们家很幸运，在蒙大拿州有处房产。而且——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh, wow. You're living the life.
turns.zh: 哦，哇。你这日子过得。

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: Yeah, very... Listen, I can't tell you how fortunate I am. And I bought this property 28 years ago, so it was a lot cheaper then.
turns.zh: 对，特别……听着，我没法告诉你我有多幸运。而且这处房产是 28 年前买的，所以当时便宜多了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: In a snowstorm, and it just felt right. But I think particularly the 1883, the precursor to Yellowstone.
turns.zh: 是在一场暴风雪里买的，当时就觉得对了。不过我尤其喜欢《1883》——就是《黄石》的前传。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I was going to ask if you saw that because that was incredible.
turns.zh: 我正想问你有没有看那个，因为那部太了不起了。

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: Yes. And then the after one, 1923, which is the post-war. 1883 really gives people a sense of what it took by those early Americans to build a life in a place like... A beautiful place but a hard, tough place like Montana. And it's just phenomenal. The person producing and writing those things is incredibly talented. Taylor Sheridan, I think, is his name.
turns.zh: 看了。然后是后面的《1923》，讲战后的。1883 真的让人感受到，那些早期美国人要在蒙大拿这种……很美、但也很苦很硬的地方建起生活，得付出什么。太震撼了。制作和编剧那些的人极有才华。我记得他叫 Taylor Sheridan。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that in the story, Montana was the easy route almost from the journey they want on.
turns.zh: 我喜欢那故事里的一点：从他们一路走来的旅程看，蒙大拿几乎算是一条轻松的路了。

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: That's right. It's very, very true, yeah.
turns.zh: 对。非常、非常真实，没错。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh, man. Yeah, you almost don't even need to watch Yellowstone. Just starting with 1883 totally works.
turns.zh: 天哪。是啊，你几乎都不用看《黄石》了。直接从《1883》开始就完全行了。

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: Yeah. In fact, I recommend people. I say there's three. But if you really want the truth about the American West, it's 1883.
turns.zh: 对。其实我也推荐人看。我说有三部。但如果你真想看美国西部的真相，那就是《1883》。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. I suggested that on this podcast a bunch, actually. So, I love that. That's where you went. (01:18:45): Next question, do you have a favorite product that you have recently discovered that you really love? Maybe one you named, maybe not.
turns.zh: 对。其实我在这个播客里安利过好多次了。所以我爱死这个了。你也是看这部。（01:18:45）下一个问题，你最近有没有发现一个特别喜欢的产品？可能是你取过名的，也可能不是。

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: I didn't name it, although it's got a very good name to it. Our whole family, I have two daughters and my wife, we're all fly fishermen, and last summer I really... I bought this for myself, but I gave it to my wife. It was one of those things that was present for her, but I knew I was going to use it more. And it's a Hardy. It's an old British fly rod, but it's a beautiful rod. It's just perfect for the big rivers of Montana. So, that's my favorite purchase.
turns.zh: 那不是我取的，不过它名字很好。我们全家——我有两个女儿和我太太——都是飞蝇钓爱好者。去年夏天我真的……这个本来是给自己买的，但我把它送给了我太太。算是个给她的礼物，但我心里清楚我会用得更多。它是 Hardy，一根老英国飞蝇竿，但特别漂亮。拿来钓蒙大拿的大河正合适。这就是我最喜欢的购物。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's the first fly-fishing rod of the podcast. Excellent choice. (01:19:24): Next question, do you have a favorite life motto that you often find yourself coming back to, sharing with friends or family?
turns.zh: 这是本播客里第一根飞蝇钓竿。绝佳选择。（01:19:24）下一个问题，你有没有一句常挂在嘴边、会跟朋友家人分享的人生格言？

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: I do. And it's a little longer, so I wrote it. I have it written here somewhere, but it's the quote from T.E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, here. And if I can find it, I should be. I think it's a wonderful quote, so I think hopefully your viewers will like this. Here's what he said. He said that, "All men dream, but not equally. Those who dream by night in the dusty recesses of their minds wake in the day to find that it was vanity, but the dreamers of the day are dangerous men for they may act on their dreams with open eyes to make them possible." (01:20:14): I read that years ago and it just hit me pretty hard, so yeah.
turns.zh: 有。而且有点长，所以我写了下来。我这儿记着呢，是 T.E. Lawrence，也就是"阿拉伯的劳伦斯"的一句话。如果我能找到……我想这是句很棒的话，希望你的观众会喜欢。他是这么说的："所有人都会做梦，但程度不同。那些夜里在脑中尘封角落做梦的人，白天醒来会发现那不过是虚妄；但白日做梦者是危险的人，因为他们睁着眼睛去践行自己的梦，让梦成为可能。"（01:20:14）我多年前读到这句话，一下子被击中了，所以确实是。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That is an amazing quote. It makes me think about the quote about the man in the arena.
turns.zh: 这金句太绝了。让我想到那句"竞技场中的人"的格言。

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: Yes. Yeah, it's same idea. It's just a little different. And I also think Lawrence of Arabia is a fascinating person, what he did. So, inspiring in some ways.
turns.zh: 对。是啊，是同样的意思，只是角度稍有不同。而且我也觉得阿拉伯的劳伦斯是个迷人人物，看他所做的事。所以在某些方面挺激励人的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: An amazing movie. (01:20:40): Okay, final question. Let me just try this. Is there a name that you didn't name that you're just like, "Wow, that was an amazing name. I wish I had come up with that name"?
turns.zh: 一部了不起的电影。（01:20:40）好，最后一个问题。让我试试这个。有没有一个不是你取的名字，让你忍不住"哇，这名字太绝了，真希望是我想出来的"？

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: I'll tell you there is one name, and it's DreamWorks. I think it's a wonderful name, and it's somewhat ironic that the entertainment industry in general has pretty mundane names. You have all of these talented people. And yet when you look at the names of production studios, movie houses, Comcast, things like that, it's very mundane. But here's DreamWorks, just like Sonos, check all the boxes. Compound dream. You expect something great from DreamWorks. They've created an experience, the experience of dreaming in a movie. I think it's a wonderful name. I wish I'd done it.
turns.zh: 我告诉你有一个，那就是 DreamWorks（梦工场）。我觉得这是个绝妙的名字，而且有点讽刺的是，整个娱乐行业用的名字都相当平庸。你有一大堆才华横溢的人，可你看那些制片厂、影业公司的名字——Comcast 之类的——都很平庸。但 DreamWorks 在这儿，和 Sonos 一样，方方面面都对了。复合词，dream（梦）。你对 DreamWorks 会期待了不起的东西。他们创造了一种体验——在电影里做梦的体验。我觉得这名字绝了。真希望是我取的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's such a cool answer. David, thank you so much for doing this. This was incredible. I learned a ton as I imagined. I feel like a lot of people are going to have a much easier time thinking about approaching this topic.
turns.zh: 这回答太酷了。David，太感谢你来做这期了。太了不起了。正如我所料，我学到了一大堆。我觉得很多人之后思考、着手这个话题，会轻松得多。

turns.speaker: David Placek
turns.en: Well, I certainly hope so. I do. It's been very, very enjoyable, very thoughtful, and I have nothing but or respect for the way you do this and the talent that you have.
